last_3_hypotheses: The LLM player exhibits fairness-seeking behavior in ultimatum-game-like prompts whenever the payoff asymmetry between proposer and responder exceeds roughly 3×; below 3×, the model accepts the asymmetric outcome.
Auto-evaluator novelty inflates by ~0.12 on the 0-1 scale when the indexed prior art is restricted to the most recent two years.
Workers that crash mid-call leave their parent_request_id orphaned in logs/orchestrator.jsonl with no terminal status entry.
proposed_hypothesis_text: The LLM player exhibits spiteful behavior (rejection of an offer that gives the responder a positive payoff but the proposer a higher one) above roughly 5× asymmetry, distinct from fairness-seeking which fires at lower asymmetries.
rationale: Same experimental setup (ultimatum-game-like prompts with payoff asymmetry) but the proposed names a different behavior (spite, not fairness) at a different threshold (5× vs 3×) and explicitly distinguishes the two. The proposed treats the prior hypothesis's claim as the contrast, not as the same finding. Distinct construct.
